Surely a boring notice about painting the street shutters.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلقي, بيلقي).

examples.trans: Let me take a look at the letter.
He took a quick look at the ledger.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إشعارات.

examples.trans: An official notice arrived in the mail.
I read the notice twice.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

بطّل.gloss: to stop (doing); no longer be able

meanings.en: to stop (doing); no longer be able
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببطل, بيبطل).

examples.trans: My knees stopped holding me up from the shock!
The rain stopped falling in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بنايات.

examples.trans: The stone building is eighty years old.
The building owner sent a letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The building is not up for sale.
The bill of sale is ready in the office.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تجارية, plural: تجاريين).

examples.trans: Converting the house into commercial offices is forbidden.
This is a residential street, not commercial.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize absolute completion or exactness.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحول, بيحول).

examples.trans: They want to turn our guesthouse into offices?
We turned the attic into a cozy guest room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخدع, بيخدع).

examples.trans: Tell me my glasses are playing tricks on me!
Appearances sometimes deceive.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباب.

examples.trans: Oh goodness, help us today!
Praise be to the Lord of all worlds.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ركب.

examples.trans: My knees got tired from climbing the stairs.
He sat on the chair to rest his knees.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رمادية, plural: رماديين).

examples.trans: He is wearing a dark grey coat.

examples.text: بدنا نحمي بيتنا من المكاتب الرمادية.
examples.trans: We want to protect our house from grey offices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عظيمة, plural: عظيمين).

examples.text: شوربة سخنة بالمطر؟ هاد شي عظيم!
examples.trans: Hot soup in the rain? That is splendid!
A great idea, everyone.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفحص, بيفحص).

examples.trans: Tariq will inspect the cellar right away.
We checked the heater and pipes this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفرح, بيفرح).

examples.trans: Let the two brothers enjoy their Friday!
We were overjoyed at the good news.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning to sit down, or sometimes to stay/remain in a place.

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشبوكة, plural: مشبوكين).

examples.text: في صفحة تانية مشبوكة ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: There is a second page clipped behind the letter.
The lamp is plugged in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مشترين.

examples.trans: The new buyers will inspect the building.
The seller and buyer agreed on the price.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معروضة, plural: معروضين).

examples.trans: The building was put up for sale.
The fresh bread is laid out on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معطية, plural: معطيين).

examples.trans: The landlord has given us thirty days.
I gave him my word yesterday.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; نقل ملكية means 'transfer of ownership / title deed'. Plural: ملكيات.

examples.trans: We read the notice of property transfer.
The title deeds are kept in the safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مملة, plural: مملين).

examples.text: تاني يوم شغل ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: Day two at work will not be boring!
We thought it was a dull municipal notice.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمشي, بيمشي).

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.

examples.text: اسمع، المي عم بتمشي جوا الماسورة!
examples.trans: Listen, the water is flowing inside the pipe!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; ألقى نظرة means 'take a look / cast a glance'. Plural: نظرات.

examples.trans: Let me take a quick look at the letter.
He spotted the problem at first glance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: We read the property transfer paper.
Moving the boxes took five minutes.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وجه لوجه means 'face to face'. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
